title: Man shot dead in Saint-Georges de Beauce: incomprehension among relatives
article: The day after the death of Guillaume Bolduc, shot by an officer of the Sûreté du Québec (SQ) in Saint-Georges de Beauce on Thursday, incomprehension reigned among his family and colleagues, who struggle to understand how he could have found himself in such a dangerous situation.

"He wasn't someone with problems, I don't know what happened. Like everyone else, we're waiting for explanations," confided the victim's mother, Sylvie Grenier, to the Journal. She cannot explain what could have happened to her son, "a guy who didn't bother anyone," in her words.
Guillaume Bolduc ended up in the middle of the street near a gas station on Lacroix Boulevard on Thursday around 7 p.m., and he seemed to be in crisis, several witnesses reported.

Then, he apparently panicked during the intervention by SQ officers, who had accidentally activated their flashing lights, according to the Bureau des enquêtes indépendantes (BEI), which is responsible for the investigation. Bolduc injured an officer with a knife, who responded by using his service weapon.

Could a psychological issue explain this behavior? The man's mother finds it hard to believe. "He was someone in perfect health. I'm telling you, a hardworking, joyful young man, who enjoyed life and nature," said Ms. Grenier, adding that she hoped to get answers quickly.

"He was a person who had deep inner suffering and who needed help," acknowledged, however, Nicole Jacques, executive director of Moisson Beauce, where Bolduc had at times used food assistance services.

Shock was also felt at his former workplace. "It's total incomprehension, unimaginable. When I was told someone had died, never in my life would I have imagined it was that guy," lamented Daniel Fortin, director of the Grand Hôtel de Saint-Georges, where Guillaume Bolduc had worked for about 10 years.

The employer is hardly consolable, just like several of his employees. On the very day of his death, Bolduc had completed his shift without showing any suspicious signs, said Mr. Fortin. "He was talking to me about his vacation that was starting next week. He was excited, he told me he was going camping," he recalled, describing a pleasant man who showed no signs of aggressiveness.

Bolduc, who still lived in the family home in Saint-Martin de Beauce, had previously faced justice for minor offenses. In 2014, he had been convicted twice of driving under the influence, and had also been arrested for drug possession.

The BEI has assigned eight of its investigators to shed light on this tragedy. They met their first witnesses yesterday. Once their work is complete, a report will be submitted to the Director of Criminal and Penal Prosecutions, who will decide whether there is reason to bring charges against the officers involved.
